comment: Section 3.7 explains that a structured, machine-readable architecture can be assessed rather than merely described. Section 5.2 nevertheless treats publication of machine-readable specifications and metadata as a forward-looking practice that may later become a readiness criterion. This limits automation of discovery, assessment and conformance even where the architecture model itself is machine-readable.

public.text: Section 3.7 explains that a structured, machine-readable architecture can be assessed rather than merely described. Section 5.2 nevertheless treats publication of machine-readable specifications and metadata as a forward-looking practice that may later become a readiness criterion. This limits automation of discovery, assessment and conformance even where the architecture model itself is machine-readable.
public.suggestedRevision: Promote machine-readable publication of component specifications and metadata from a forward-looking observation to a SHOULD-level requirement, with appropriate maturity exceptions. Add the requirement to the component descriptions in Appendix C and cross-reference section 3.7.
